nodes.label: Daily Strategy Candidate Events Table Schema
Scanner Candidate Defines Where to Look
nodes.rationale: Scanner outputs define an observable candidate denominator and ranking surface, not event truth, market state, labels, strategy signals, or complete universe membership.

nodes.label: Observable State Excludes Future Outcomes
nodes.rationale: Market and event state must preserve only legal as-of observables; outcome, label, reward, action, fill, PnL, and future namespaces remain prohibited and join separately.

nodes.label: Quote-Guarded View Preserves Raw Lineage
nodes.rationale: The quote-guarded price view overlays an immutable raw 1m source with an explicit repair manifest rather than silently correcting raw history in place.

nodes.label: Explicit As-Of Cutoff Controls Consumption
nodes.rationale: Context sources are legal only when their declared availability timestamp or date is not later than the event or decision cutoff.

nodes.label: Materialized Does Not Mean Unrestricted
nodes.rationale: A table may exist physically while remaining scoped, provisional, blocked for direct ML/RL, or unsuitable as execution truth; consumer gates remain authoritative.

nodes.label: State Component Is Not the State
nodes.rationale: Fundamentals, news, regime, short context, scanners, and other governed inputs remain components until a state builder composes them under a common decision-time cutoff.

nodes.label: Consumption Legality Is Independent of State Role
nodes.rationale: A pre-event or at-event role is not sufficient for predictive use; decision-safe legality and dataset-specific consumer gates must also pass.

nodes.label: Registry Metadata Is Not Promotion
nodes.rationale: A registry records artifact identity, lineage, current evidence, and permitted consumers; it does not override scoped, provisional, or blocked status declared by contracts and policies.

nodes.label: Component Cutoffs Compose Legal State
nodes.rationale: A legal market-state row requires every included component to satisfy its own availability, lag, namespace, quality, and decision-time cutoff rules.

nodes.label: Outcomes Are Y, Not X
nodes.rationale: Every outcome row contains post-event information and therefore belongs on the label side of a separate join, never in the pre-event feature state.

Base eligible, in-play, and strategy overlay separation
nodes.rationale: Separating the base-eligible denominator, the in-play momentum denominator, and strategy overlays prevents sequential scanner filters from silently redefining the research population.

nodes.label: Scanner, event, window, state, and outcome separation
nodes.rationale: Scanner candidates identify where to look, event candidates record what occurred and its legal anchor, windows bound observation, state records decision-time observables, and outcomes remain separate labels.

nodes.label: Decision-time composition boundary
nodes.rationale: A legal state row may compose only components that satisfy the declared decision cutoff, lag, namespace, and consumer gate; future outcomes, labels, and rewards cannot enter the observable state.

nodes.label: Repair overlay instead of raw rewrite
nodes.rationale: The quote-guarded candidate preserves immutable raw one-minute bars and applies only promoted repairs through a traceable overlay, keeping raw and corrected views distinct.

Canonical state versus representation layer contract
No blind full-universe materialization
nodes.rationale: A broad materialization requires an explicit denominator, source roots, reconciliation, manifests, quality gates, and promotion evidence; pointing a scoped builder at a larger folder is not sufficient.

nodes.label: Observable truth precedes representation
nodes.rationale: Canonical state preserves neutral, legally observable inputs, while semantic or latent representations remain versioned downstream candidates and cannot rewrite source truth.

nodes.label: State X and outcome y separation
nodes.rationale: Decision-time state is feature input X, while post-event returns, MFE, MAE, labels, and rewards are downstream y and must never be embedded in pre-decision state rows.

nodes.label: Quote-guarded overlay preserves raw authority
nodes.rationale: The quote-guarded view combines immutable raw one-minute bars with a promoted repair manifest overlay, preserving both original observations and repair lineage without rewriting raw data.

nodes.label: Expected denominator is not observed presence
nodes.rationale: A structurally coherent expectation calendar defines what should exist; it does not prove that daily, minute, quote, or trade observations are physically present or valid.

nodes.label: Post-event state is not decision-safe
nodes.rationale: Post-event review rows contain information unavailable at the earlier decision boundary and must not be marked decision-safe or used as pre-decision ML features.

nodes.label: Scoped candidate does not imply promotion
nodes.rationale: Passing controlled candidate checks establishes the declared scoped evidence only; it does not grant official, full-universe, ML, RL, backtest, or execution authority.

nodes.label: Eligibility is not in-play selection
nodes.rationale: The base denominator identifies common-stock small-cap rows eligible for observation; a separate governed movement and tradability rule is required before a row becomes an in-play candidate.

nodes.label: Intraday in-play momentum candidate denominator v0.1
First-cross timing requires intraday data
nodes.rationale: Premarket, regular-session, and after-hours first-cross timing must be derived from as-of one-minute bars; a daily end-of-day proxy cannot certify when the frontside move occurred.

nodes.label: Top-N ranking requires a minimum motion threshold
nodes.rationale: Ranking alone can select economically irrelevant rows, so percent-change candidates must pass a declared minimum move before top-N selection.

nodes.label: Daily RVOL is not intraday volume acceleration
nodes.rationale: The intended relative-volume signal is recent-bar, intraday, as-of acceleration; a daily RVOL proxy is only builder-shape evidence and must remain unavailable or provisional.

nodes.label: Scanner candidate is not market state
nodes.rationale: Scanner configs define governed candidate surfaces; they contain no labels, outcomes, rewards, fills, PnL, or strategy decisions and cannot substitute for market-state or event-state tables.

nodes.label: Independent adversarial validation
nodes.rationale: Institutionalization requires independent schema, manifest, source-reconciliation, external-evidence, and mutation tests that fail under injected defects; a builder cannot certify itself.
